subject: Dedicated pool throughput warranty and queueing behavior — Helios AI
messages:
From: contracts@helios.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: throughput warranty and preemption behavior for Dedicated Pool

Hi Lauren / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward a committed Dedicated pool for Helios, the procurement team has one specific ask: can Redwood provide a clear "throughput warranty" we can rely on in our contract?

Concretely, we need language that defines:
- What "throughput warranty" means for reserved GPUs (tokens/sec or inference units sustained over what window),
- How queueing behaves when a tenant uses burst capacity (preemption order, notification, and expected wait time),
- What remedies or credits are available if throughput falls below the warranty for more than X minutes.

I've attached a draft SLA from our side (helios-draft-sla.pdf) that shows the kind of warranty/credit structure procurement is comfortable with. We aren't asking for firm numbers yet — just clarity on definitions and whether Redwood can commit to a warranty-like clause, or if you treat these as operational SLOs only.

Can you respond with suggested warranty semantics and an outline of how queueing/preemption would be documented in contract language? If it helps, Elaine (cc'd on this thread) can jump on a call this afternoon.

Thanks,
Elaine Cho
Contracts Manager
Helios AI
attachments: helios-draft-sla.pdf
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: contracts@helios.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: throughput warranty and preemption behavior for Dedicated Pool

Elaine —

Appreciate the clear ask and the draft SLA. I'm including Ben (sales/solutions) and David (technical PM for Dedicated runtime) so we can cover commercial and operational sides. High level: Redwood is comfortable documenting a deterministic expectation for sustained throughput on reserved capacity, but we typically express guarantees in terms of measurable SLOs (e.g., 99th percentile throughput over a 5m/1h window) and pair that with a remediation/credit structure.

Next steps: Ben and David will propose concrete semantics (units, measurement windows, preemption ordering) and a short piece of contract language we can iterate on. Can you confirm the Helios comfort zone for remediation (credit cap as % of monthly committed spend) so we align on ranges?

I'll leave the technical details to Ben/David. If a call today works, share a 30-min slot and we'll do it.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: throughput warranty and preemption behavior for Dedicated Pool

Elaine / Lauren / team —

Thanks — I took a pass based on how we operationalize Dedicated. Below is a concise framing we think maps to both engineering controls and contract language. We can turn the bulleted items into a one-paragraph warranty and a measurement appendix.

1) Terminology (how we would define the warranty)
- "Reserved throughput warranty": the minimum sustained processing rate (in tokens/sec or inference requests/sec) guaranteed per reserved GPU-equivalent instance, measured at the per-tenant level.
- Measurement window options: rolling 5-minute, 1-hour, and daily aggregates. Typical warranty candidates: 5-minute 99th percentile and 1-hour median.

2) Queueing & preemption behavior
- Dedicated pool: tenants are guaranteed access to reserved slots that provide the above throughput under normal operations.
- Bursting: if tenant workload exceeds reserved capacity, requests will enter the tenant's dedicated queue and can be served from shared burst capacity subject to availability.
- Preemption order: preemptions are based on priority tiers (Reserved > Burst-committed > Spot). Preemption is last-in-first-out within the burst tier; preemption events are announced by a 30s in-band header on streaming responses and an async audit event.
- Expected wait time: when burst is exhausted, median queue wait is typically < 6s for workloads with median seq len <= 512 tokens; we will include a measurement appendix for Helios's expected distribution.

3) Remedies and credits
- Remediation trigger: sustained violation where measured throughput falls below the warranty for more than 30 continuous minutes in a 24-hour period.
- Credit structure: pro-rated credits against committed monthly reservation fee; suggested default: 5% credit for first trigger, 15% for repeat triggers within billing month, capped at 30%. We can adjust caps to align to procurement guidance.

4) Measurement & auditability
- Redundantly measured by the Redwood control plane and exposed as per-tenant time series (tokens/sec, requests/sec, tail-latency histograms).
- We propose a signed weekly extract for the first 90 days of the contract if Helios wants extra auditability.

Attachments: I attached a short CSV with sample throughput metrics and a draft warranty terms doc (redwood-throughput-metrics.csv, warranty-terms-draft.docx).

If those semantics look reasonable, we'll craft a single warranty paragraph and an appendix with measurement queries + a short runbook describing queueing behavior and notification hooks.

We can also run a 72-hour pre-commitment soak test against a non-prod pool to validate numbers. What range for credit caps would keep procurement satisfied (ballpark % of committed spend)?

- Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-throughput-metrics.csv; warranty-terms-draft.docx

Ben / Lauren —

This is helpful, thank you. Procurement will want a warranty paragraph (we prefer deterministic language over purely operational SLOs) plus a measurement appendix that maps to exact queries our auditors can run. The suggested credit caps look within the ballpark — procurement's initial guidance is a 10% ceiling for single incidents and 25% monthly cap, so your suggested defaults are close.

We'd like the 72-hour pre-commitment soak test you proposed, and we'd prefer the measurement appendix to include the exact Prometheus queries or BigQuery export schema we should expect. Can you draft the warranty paragraph today and circulate a measurement appendix? We'll review and schedule the soak test for next week.

Also, please include a short statement about maintenance windows and how planned maintenance affects the warranty (we expect routine maintenance to be excluded from remediation triggers if prior notice is given).

I'll follow up with a DocuSign request once we have the warranty paragraph. Thanks — Elaine
